test: Spearman correlation over the simulated targets between memorability (hit rate minus false alarm rate) in Simulation 1 (within category, criterion 20) and Simulation 2 (across categories, criterion 5); seed 47826, 1,000 runs per category within and 1,000 runs across; false alarms: in every run each studied target is probed against 30 newly generated and stored lure items and counts as a false alarm when the mean likelihood ratio exceeds the criterion

Spearman correlation over the simulated targets between memorability in Simulation 1 (within category) and summed similarity within category; summed similarity = minus the mean Euclidean distance to the other 299 items of the target's category (within) or to the other 6,299 items (across); higher = less distinctive; a negative rho means that the more distinctive targets are the more memorable ones

Spearman correlation over the simulated targets between memorability in Simulation 2 (across categories) and summed similarity across categories; summed similarity = minus the mean Euclidean distance to the other 299 items of the target's category (within) or to the other 6,299 items (across); higher = less distinctive; a negative rho means that the more distinctive targets are the more memorable ones

Spearman correlation over the simulated targets between summed similarity within category and across categories; summed similarity = minus the mean Euclidean distance to the other 299 items of the target's category (within) or to the other 6,299 items (across); higher = less distinctive; p is below the smallest double-precision number (scipy and MATLAB return 0) and is computed through its logarithm, log10 p = -681.24
